p: Millo in the: He made a double wall.
city of David: Read 2Sa 5:9.
darts and shields in abundance: Some read, swords or daggers.
arm of flesh: That is, the power of man.
LORD our God to help us: This declares that Hezekiah always put his trust in God, and yet made himself strong and used lawful means, lest he should seem to tempt God.
against Lachish: While he besieged Lachish.

altars: Thus the wicked put no difference between true religion and false, God and idols: for Hezekiah only destroyed idolatry and replaced it with true religion. Thus the papists slander the servants of God: for when they destroy idolatry, they say that they abolish religion.
gods of those nations that my: This is his blasphemy that he will compare the living God to vile idols.
mine hand: When man has prosperity, he swells in pride, and thinks himself able to resist and overcome even God himself.
servant Hezekiah: In this we see that when the wicked speak evil of the servants of God, they care not to blaspheme God himself for if they feared God, they would love his servants.
cried with a loud voice in: Their words are written, 2Ki 18:19.
work of the hands of man: Which were invented, made and authorized by man.
prayed and cried to heaven: This shows what the best refuge in all troubles and dangers is.
captains in the camp of the: To the number of 185,000 as in 2Ki 19:35,36.
own bowels slew him there with: Meaning, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons.
magnified in the sight of all: Thus after trouble God sends comfort to all them who patiently wait on him, and constantly put their trust in his mercies.
a sign: To confirm his faith in God's promise, who declared to him by his prophet that his life would be prolonged fifteen years.
was lifted up: He was lifted up with the pride of his victory and treasures, and shows them for an ostentation to the ambassadors of Babylon.
Gihon: Which also was called Shiloh, of which mention is made in Isa 8:6, Joh 9:7.

try him: Here we see the reason why the faithful are tempted, which is to determine whether they have faith or not, and that they may feel the presence of God who does not allow them to be overcome by temptations, but in their weakness administers strength.
